# Section heading

> The heading block every section opens with: a display title that draws its own brand period, an optional intro line, and small mono labels for sub-sections.

Part of the [Nate Mills Design System](../README.md). It is a CSS class API, not a JavaScript component, so its props are the classes and HTML attributes below. Link the stylesheets as [Getting started](../foundations/getting-started.md) shows, then add the classes. Every component: [Components](../COMPONENTS.md).

## When to use

- The start of every page section.
- A one-line intro under a section title.
- A small label for a sub-section further down the page.

## When not to use

- A card title: use a plain heading inside the Card.
- An eyebrow above the section title: that tier was retired.

## Alternatives

- **[Chip](chip.md):** A section label names a part of the page; a Chip labels a thing inside it. Neither is clickable.

## How to use

**Element:** `<div class="section-head">` around an `<h2 class="section-title">` (an `<h3>` inside a section), a `<p class="section-subtitle">`, and `<p class="section-label">` for a sub-section label.

- Wrap the title in `.section-head` and put `.section-title` on the heading element.
- Put `.section-subtitle` on the intro `<p>`.
- Put `.section-label` on a sub-section label `<p>`, with a variant class only when the layout needs it.

**Classes:** `.section-head`, `.section-label`, `.section-label--accent`, `.section-label--center`, `.section-label--icon`, `.section-label--row`, `.section-title`, `.section-subtitle`

## Props

| Prop | Type | Allowed values | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | element | `h2`, `h3`, or any heading level | `h2` for a page section | The heading element under `.section-title`, picked for where it sits: `h3` inside a section. |
| `label variant` | modifier class | `accent` (`.section-label--accent`), `center` (`.section-label--center`), `icon` (`.section-label--icon`), `row` (`.section-label--row`) | No class: a left-aligned inline label. | Applies to `.section-label` only. `.section-title`, `.section-subtitle` and `.section-head` take no modifiers. |

## Variants

Available label variants: `accent`, `center`, `icon`, `row`.

- `accent` (`.section-label--accent`): Accent-emphasis colour, for labels on marquee cards.
- `center` (`.section-label--center`): Centred.
- `icon` (`.section-label--icon`): Led by a decorative glyph.
- `row` (`.section-label--row`): A full-width heading row rather than an inline tag.

Default label variant: No class: a left-aligned inline label.

## States

No interactive states: a section heading is text and never takes a click or focus.

## Invalid combinations

Options that must not be used together. Each names the props above.

| Combination | Level | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `.section-title` with a typed full stop at the end | MUST NOT | The `::after` already draws the brand period, so it doubles. |
| `.section-label` directly above a `.section-title` | MUST NOT | That eyebrow tier was retired; the label is for sub-sections. |
| `.section-head` with a top margin on the element after it | MUST NOT | The block owns that gap. |
| `label variant` on `.section-title`, `.section-subtitle` or `.section-head` | MUST NOT | Only `.section-label` takes the variants. |

## Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Passes over it: a section heading is not focusable. |
| Enter, Space | Do nothing: a section heading takes no input. |
| H in a screen reader's browse mode (VoiceOver: VO + Command + H) | Moves to the next heading. `.section-title` sits on a real `<h2>` or `<h3>`, so it is in the list. |
| 2 or 3 in browse mode (NVDA, JAWS) | Moves to the next heading at that level. |
| Down arrow in a screen reader's browse mode (VoiceOver: VO + Right arrow) | Reads the title, then the `.section-subtitle` intro. The brand period is drawn by CSS and is not read. |

Screen-reader users reach headings with their heading navigation, not Tab.

## Rules

| Level | Rule | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| MUST NOT | Type a full stop after a `.section-title`. | [Automated: Component-rules lint](../foundations/checks.md#component-rules-lint) |
| MUST | Let `.section-head` own the gap below the heading; add no top margin to what follows. | [Automated: Section-head gate](../foundations/checks.md#section-head-gate) |
| SHOULD | Pick the heading level for where it sits: `<h2>` for a page section, `<h3>` inside one. | [Automated: Screen-reader structure gate](../foundations/checks.md#screen-reader-structure-gate) |

Automated checks run on natemills.me before every publish; the scripts live in the private source repository.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Let `.section-head` own the gap below a heading, and declare no top margin on the content that follows it.
- Let `.section-title` draw its own brand period; the dot is an `::after`, never a typed full stop in the markup.
- Let `.section-title` keep its own box while it draws; the drawing is laid over it, which is what keeps it in the screen reader list.
- Hold `.section-title` at its 22ch measure and `.section-subtitle` at 60ch; both are set for reading, not for filling the width.

### Don't

- Do not add a top margin under `.section-head`; the component owns that gap and `--section-head-gap` is the only dial.
- Do not put a `.section-label` above a `.section-title`; that eyebrow tier was retired and the class is a sub-section label now.
- Do not type a full stop after `.section-title`, because its `::after` already draws the brand period.
- Do not scroll-scrub a heading outside the page flow; a specimen in a tab panel takes `data-hc-manual` and replays on a press.

## Example

```html
<div class="section-head">
  <h2 class="section-title">Training</h2>
</div>
<p class="section-label">Degree</p>
```

## Classes

| Class | Kind | What it does | Tokens it reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.section-head` | base | wrapper | `--section-head-gap` |
| `.section-label` | base | uppercase mono eyebrow | `--chip-line`, `--color-text-tertiary`, `--font-feature-mono`, `--font-mono`, `--space-200`, `--text-label`, `--tracking-eyebrow`, `--weight-semibold` |
| `.section-label--accent` | modifier | accent-emphasis colour, for eyebrows on marquee cards | `--color-accent-emphasis` |
| `.section-label--center` | modifier | centred | None |
| `.section-label--icon` | modifier | icon-led; the glyph is decorative | None |
| `.section-label--row` | modifier | heading ROW rather than an inline tag | None |
| `.section-title` | base | any heading level, picked for where it sits (h2 for a page section, h3 inside one); carries the drawn brand period | `--brand-primary`, `--color-text-primary`, `--display-section`, `--display-tight`, `--dot-radius`, `--font-display`, `--line-display`, `--space-300`, `--weight-extrabold` |
| `.section-subtitle` | base | intro line under the title | `--color-text-secondary`, `--font-body`, `--line-body`, `--space-500`, `--text-body` |

## Tokens

Every token the classes above read, as data from tokens.json: write `var(--name)`, never the raw value. A component token belongs to one component: change it to restyle that component and nothing else. A semantic token is a shared role; never change one for a single component. The three tiers: [Tokens](../foundations/tokens.md#three-tiers).

| Token | Tier | Value | What it is for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--chip-line` | Component | `1.4` | Chip label line height. Component-level literal, sized to the mono label; off the named line scale by design. |
| `--brand-primary` | Semantic | `#d2ff37`, from `--lime-500` | The brand lime, scarce on purpose: the primary button fill, brand outlines, focus rings on dark surfaces and status dots. Never body text on a light surface. |
| `--color-accent-emphasis` | Semantic | `#1c1c1f`; dark `#d2ff37`, from `--neutral-850` | Theme-aware emphasis text following the accent role: ink on light, lime on dark. For text on theme-following surfaces; on-* tokens are for fixed-colour surfaces. |
| `--color-text-primary` | Semantic | `#0a0a0b`; dark `#f4f4f5`, from `--neutral-950` | Default reading text. Near-black on light, near-white on dark. |
| `--color-text-secondary` | Semantic | `#3f3f46`; dark `#a1a1aa`, from `--neutral-700` | Secondary text: supporting copy one step quieter than text-primary. |
| `--color-text-tertiary` | Semantic | `#67676f`; dark `#909096`, from `--neutral-600` | Tertiary text: section labels and quiet meta copy; the last step that still clears 4.5:1 on light. |
| `--display-section` | Semantic | `clamp(min(4.25rem, 19vw), 8.7vw, 7.5rem)` | Section headings (every section h2). .section-title consumes this; the About headings are a documented exception in sections.css (Hi, I'm Nate opens the section and fills its column; the headline over the story fills its column and stays under 85% of it). |
| `--display-tight` | Semantic | `-0.0176em` | Display tracking. Pairs with every heading above card size, the hero included. |
| `--dot-radius` | Semantic | `999px`, from `--radius-full` | Circle geometry: dots, markers, slider thumbs, and drawn circles (the brand period, status dots, touch-target rings). Full by definition: a re-theme that softens buttons leaves a dot round, and the theme lab's corner tier squares it only when the whole system goes sharp (0 at sharp, full at soft and round). |
| `--font-body` | Semantic | `"Work Sans", "Work Sans Fallback", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif` | Body copy, lists, and buttons. |
| `--font-display` | Semantic | `"Anton", Impact, "Haettenschweiler", sans-serif` | Display headings and large numbers. Anton, one weight, never faux-bolded. |
| `--font-feature-mono` | Semantic | `"zero" 1` | Switches on the slashed zero for every piece of mono text. |
| `--font-mono` | Semantic | `"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace` | Tabular numbers, code, and eyebrow labels. |
| `--line-body` | Semantic | `1.5` | Default reading text: paragraphs, lists, captions. The workhorse. |
| `--line-display` | Semantic | `1.05` | Display-grade headings (--text-h1, section h2s). Big text wants the tightest leading. |
| `--section-head-gap` | Semantic | `clamp(var(--space-300), 1.75vw, var(--space-500))` | Section rhythm. The single gap from a section heading to the first content under it, owned by .section-head. |
| `--space-200` | Semantic | `8px` | Tight gap. Chip padding, small stacks. |
| `--space-300` | Semantic | `12px` | Medium-tight break. Heading-to-body, compact rows. |
| `--space-500` | Semantic | `24px` | Medium break. Group separation inside a section; the standard card-padding tier (--card-pad-standard). |
| `--text-body` | Semantic | `1rem`, from `--size-base` | Paragraphs, lists, default reading text, card body copy. |
| `--text-label` | Semantic | `0.6875rem`, from `--size-2xs` | Uppercase mono labels, eyebrows, stat labels, badges. |
| `--tracking-eyebrow` | Semantic | `0.18em` | Wide tracking for uppercase eyebrows. |
| `--weight-extrabold` | Semantic | `800` | Five distinct weights. The body face loads 400 to 800 as one variable file; the display face ships a single 400, so font-synthesis is off site-wide. |
| `--weight-semibold` | Semantic | `600` | 600. The workhorse emphasis: buttons, subheads, labels. |
